abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has a five-year survival rate below 10%. Most cases are unresectable, and treatment is hampered by dense stroma, an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a minimally invasive modality that kills tumor cells via reactive oxygen species and may modulate immunoregulatory molecules. The effect of zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc)-mediated PDT on immune checkpoint expression in PDAC has not been characterized.
METHODS: Immune checkpoint gene expression was compared between pancreatic tumor and normal tissue using TCGA-PAAD and GTEx datasets via GEPIA2. MIA PaCa-2 and PANC-1 cell lines were treated with ZnPc-PDT (675 nm; 80 mW; 12 J/cm2). Cytotoxicity was measured by MTT assay, apoptosis and cell-cycle distribution were analyzed by flow cytometry, and transcript levels of CD47, CTLA-4, PD-L1, and VISTA, together with the apoptosis-related genes BAX and BCL2, were quantified by RT-qPCR and normalized to GAPDH.
RESULTS: In silico analysis showed significantly higher expression of CD47, CTLA-4, and VISTA in PDAC than in normal pancreas, whereas the difference for PD-L1 was not significant. ZnPc alone showed no cytotoxicity; light activation produced dose-dependent cell death with IC50 values of 0.784 μg/mL (MIA PaCa-2) and 0.09 μg/mL (PANC-1). Flow cytometric analysis showed that ZnPc-PDT significantly increased the percentage of apoptotic cells in both cell lines. Cell-cycle analysis revealed an increase in the sub-G1 fraction in both cell lines. MIA PaCa-2 cells also showed a modest but significant increase in the G0/G1 fraction. ZnPc-PDT increased BAX and decreased BCL2 transcript levels in both cell lines. Treatment with ZnPc-PDT significantly downregulated CD47, CTLA-4, and PD-L1 transcript levels in both cell lines, whereas VISTA was downregulated only in PANC-1 cells.
CONCLUSIONS: ZnPc-PDT induced light-dependent cytotoxicity and consistently downregulated the transcript levels of CD47, CTLA-4, and PD-L1 in PDAC cells, while VISTA regulation is cell-line dependent. These in vitro findings warrant protein-level and immune-functional validation before combinations of PDT with immune checkpoint inhibitors are explored for PDAC.
key_points_ko: ZnPc-PDT는 췌장암 세포주 MIA PaCa-2와 PANC-1에서 각각 IC50 0.784 μg/mL 및 0.09 μg/mL의 세포 독성을 보였습니다.
치료 후 두 세포주 모두에서 세포사멸 촉진 유전자(BAX) 전사체는 증가하고 억제 유전자(BCL2) 전사체는 감소했습니다.
ZnPc-PDT 치료는 두 췌장암 세포주 모두에서 CD47, CTLA-4, PD-L1 면역관문 유전자의 전사체 수준을 유의미하게 하향 조절했습니다.
summary_ko: 췌장암 세포주에서 아연 프탈로시아닌(ZnPc)을 활용한 광역학 치료(PDT)의 효과를 평가한 기초 전임상 연구입니다. ZnPc-PDT는 빛 조사 조건에서 췌장암 세포의 아포토시스(apoptosis, 세포사멸)를 효과적으로 유도했습니다. 또한 주요 면역관문(immune checkpoint) 유전자인 CD47, CTLA-4, PD-L1의 전사체 발현을 유의미하게 줄였습니다. 본 연구는 향후 광역학 치료와 면역항암제 병용 치료법의 가능성을 세포 수준에서 제시합니다.
title: Photodynamic therapy induces apoptosis and downregulates immune checkpoint transcripts in pancreatic cancer cells
title_ko: 광역학 치료가 췌장암 세포의 세포사멸을 유도하고 면역관문 전사체 발현을 감소시킴
